newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai port tonnages rise seven percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Dubai port tonnages rise seven percent in 1996.

text.p: Dubai Ports Authority said volumes handled at its twin terminals of Port Rashid and Jebel Ali rose seven percent in 1996 to 30 million tonnes.
The number of standard container units handled in the year rose eight percent to a record 2.25 million from 2.07 million in 1995, it added in a statement.

DPA chairman Sultan bin Sulayem said transhipment business, which made up about half container cargo handling, was expected to grow this year "because of the increase in feeder ship requirements to developing areas such as India, and also to the southern republics of the former Soviet Union."
He said increasing volumes of containers were coming through Dubai ports for onward shipment to Iran's Bandar Abbas and then, by road, to the southern Commonwealth of Independent States.

With the introduction of large container ships, particularly the new generation of 6,000 TEU capacity, and increased competition among lines "there will be significant rationalisation in the number of ports served, with only one or two per region," Sulayem said.
"As far as the Middle East is concerned, this trend will focus more attention on Dubai," he added.
Shipping industry executives have said Dubai could face stiff long-term competition from Oman's Mina Raysut and Yemen's Aden, which are being developed.
Both ports, seeking to secure their status as a mid-point between East and West, remove the need for two days extra sailing time through the Strait of Hormuz.
